audit.whatIsWrong: Maokai's abilities are never named and his sustain is treated as passive scenery.
audit.why: Sap Magic's cooldown drops every time he casts a spell or is struck by one, so poking him actually speeds up his heal — the reason chip alone never gets him low.
audit.corrected: Chip does not accumulate: every Avengerang you land shortens Sap Magic's cooldown, so trade in bursts that beat one heal, not in trickles.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 and late spikes give no cooldowns.
audit.why: Twisted Advance is 14/13/12/11/10s and Nature's Grasp is 130/110/90s; his all-in is gated on a 14-second dash, which is the number that decides whether you can step up.
audit.corrected: Level 6: his all-in is Twisted Advance (14s at rank 1) into Bramble Smash — step up on that cooldown, not on his health bar.

audit.whatIsWrong: Twisted Advance's untargetability is absent, and the anti-heal requirement is never stated.
audit.why: Maokai is untargetable for the whole Twisted Advance dash, so a Comeuppance lock-on or a queued Avengerang is wasted if you fire as he commits; Sap Magic plus his health scaling make Grievous Wounds the item that decides extended fights.
audit.corrected: Twisted Advance makes him untargetable in flight — never spend R or Q into the dash; buy Grievous Wounds before the first tank item lands.

edits.before: His W root-dash into Q is his cleanest all-in window — if it lands while you're away from a wall, you can't E-escape and your R channel gets interrupted by the root.
edits.after: Twisted Advance (14s) into Bramble Smash is his cleanest all-in — he is untargetable for the whole dash, so a fired R is wasted and the root then cuts your channel.

edits.before: Two tank items in, his sapling sustain and raw HP outscale your lethality — your missing-health R execute stops one-shotting and he tanks your full rotation.
edits.after: Two tank items in, Sap Magic sustain and raw HP outscale your lethality — without Grievous Wounds your missing-health R stops closing and he tanks a full rotation.

edits.before: Heal your Q chip with passive sustain and saplings, then trade back when your E and R are down
edits.after: Heal your chip with Sap Magic — every spell he casts or is struck by shortens its cooldown

edits.before: His passive sustain and saplings heal your Q chip, so neither side converts cleanly — it's a spacing duel around his W and your terrain.
edits.after: Sap Magic's cooldown shrinks every time you hit him, so chip never accumulates — it's a spacing duel around Twisted Advance and your terrain.

edits.before: Your R threatens a low Maokai, but his W root pins you and interrupts the channel, and E only escapes toward walls — the kill threat cuts both ways.
edits.after: Your R threatens a low Maokai, but he is untargetable through Twisted Advance and the root then cuts the channel — the kill threat cuts both ways.

edits.before: This is a genuine coin-flip window. Your Q poke and the passive shield from every third stack let you trade into him, but his passive sustain and saplings heal the chip right back, so you rarely get him low without a hard commit. At 6 his W root into Q is his cleanest all-in — if it catches you off a wall with E unusable, the root interrupts your R channel and he wins the flip. Only go for the R execute when his W is on cooldown and you have terrain behind you for the E bail-out.
edits.after: This is a genuine coin-flip window. Your Q poke and the passive shield from every third stack let you trade into him, but Sap Magic's cooldown shortens every time you land a spell on him, so chip alone never gets him low without a hard commit. At 6 Twisted Advance (14s) into Bramble Smash is his all-in — he is untargetable for the whole dash, so never fire R into it, and off a wall the root cuts your channel. Go for the execute only on that dash's cooldown.

notes: The kit file's derived 'grounding' flag on Bramble Smash contradicts Riot's description (knockback plus slow only), so I did not claim it stops Heroic Swing. Sapling Toss is 1100 range and stronger in brush — worth remembering before a Going Rogue brush roam, though the kit does not state that it reveals camouflage, so I left that claim out.
